question: A trainer asks Claude for two onboarding guides on the same topic: one for new hires with no industry background and one for experienced hires from a competitor. What distinguishes an effective adaptation between the two versions?
options: A) Both versions include identical content, differing only in the order the sections appear
B) The experienced-hire version repeats every foundational term twice for reinforcement
C) The new-hire version uses a more casual tone while the experienced version drops all punctuation
D) The new-hire version defines foundational terms that the experienced version can assume the reader knows
correct_answers: D) The new-hire version defines foundational terms that the experienced version can assume the reader knows
explanations: Incorrect. Reordering identical content without adjusting explained context does not address the different background knowledge of each audience.
Incorrect. Repeating foundational terms for experienced hires adds unnecessary content for readers who already understand that vocabulary.
Incorrect. Removing punctuation does not adapt content to audience background and would harm readability for either group.
Correct. Adapting for prior background means adjusting how much foundational context is spelled out, assuming less for readers with no experience and more for those who already know it.
